newsitem.title: UK: UK Royal Mail, union agree to hold peace talks.
newsitem.headline: UK Royal Mail, union agree to hold peace talks.

text.p: The Royal Mail said on Monday it would hold talks with union representatives in the next few days in a bid to resolve two separate disputes over discipline which led London-based postal workers to hold strikes over the weekend.
"We are happy to talk (with the union)...strikes don't help anyone. We want to get these disputes resolved," a spokesman for the state-run Royal Mail said in an interview.
A spokesman for the main union involved in the disputes was not immediately available for comment.

Some 1,000 Communication Workers Union (CWU) members staged a walkout at a central London delivery office on Friday over sackings which, the union argues, breach a national agreement. The strike ends later today.
Separately, 200 CWU members working at a distribution centre in north-west London also went on strike on Friday over disciplinary action taken by management.
Both disputes hit mail coming in and out of London over the weekend, but the Royal Mail said it was able to keep some services running by hiring casual workers.
